subject: Post-demo: ClearBeam performance criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@clearbeam.com>, Mike Coleman <mike.coleman@clearbeam.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: ClearBeam performance criteria & next steps

Thanks again for carving out time today — great conversation. Per request, attaching a concise SLO matrix and the demo logs we captured for the baseline run. Quick recap of what we heard and the items we need you to confirm so we can size the pilot/canary: 

1) SLO targets (your ask)
- Tail latency: 99th pct P95-window target = 300ms for inference responses over streaming end-to-end (app->Redwood->client).
- Throughput: sustain 1,200 requests/minute aggregate (~20 RPS) with 40 concurrent sessions.
- Burst / peak: handle short bursts up to 120 concurrent active sessions for 3–5 minutes without cold-start slowdowns.
- Token-rate streaming: average outbound streaming rate ~250 tokens/sec during peak flows.

2) Workload notes we collected
- Typical input sequence length: 350 tokens average, up to 1,100 tokens in worst-case batch.
- Mixed read/write workload: 85% generate/chat, 15% embedding/rerank calls to separate route.
- Sensitive PII flows in a small subset of traffic — will require private VPC path for pilot (you flagged compliance).

3) Proposed immediate next steps (action owners)
- ClearBeam: confirm SLO numbers above or provide adjusted targets by EOD Tue (Sara).
- Redwood (Alex): provide a one-week canary plan + cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted within 24h of SLO confirmation.
- Redwood (Karthik): pre-provision a staging pool and share a test harness for load scripts (by Apr 28).
- ClearBeam: provide a list of 5 representative prompts and a short sample dataset (anonymized) for regression checks.

Attachments: clearbeam_slo_matrix.xlsx (SLO rows + measurement plan), rdw-demo-logs-20270425.zip (demo traces), post-demo-runbook.md (checklist).

If the numbers above look off, flag the specific item (latency vs concurrency vs streaming rate) — that'll change the deployment recommendation (e.g., go Dedicated with higher reserved capacity vs Hosted + autoscale).

Thanks — I can hop on a quick 20-min sync tomorrow if helpful.

— Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@clearbeam.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Coleman <mike.coleman@clearbeam.com>, Procurement <procurement@clearbeam.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ClearBeam performance criteria & next steps

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and the artifacts. Quick confirmations from our side and one clarification: 

- Latency: 99th pct <= 300ms is our stretch goal for interactive features (physician UI). If you can demonstrate 99th <= 400ms with fallbacks, that's acceptable for MVP. So please capture both 300ms (preferred) and 400ms (acceptable).
- Throughput & concurrency: the 1,200 req/min and 40 concurrent sessions are representative of our first-phase rollout. We will likely need to scale to ~80 concurrent in week 4 of pilot, so please include an elasticity check in your canary plan.
- Streaming tokens: 250 tokens/sec peak is fine — we have a handful of sessions with higher rates (up to 450 tokens/sec) when diagnostic transcripts stream overnight; call that a low-priority long-tail case.

Actioning items from ClearBeam:
- I'll upload the anonymized prompt set and a short sample to the secure SharePoint link by EOD Monday.
- Procurement looped in here for contract/terms and needs an estimated committed capacity and a one-page security note (SOC2 scope + VPC options).

Question: when you say "KV cache" in the SLO matrix, does that assume cold-start miss penalty? For our burst profile we care about warm cache behavior. If we can warm the KV layer in advance (pre-warming step), what delta in 99th latency do you typically see?

Thanks — Sara
Director of Product, ClearBeam Health
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@clearbeam.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@clearbeam.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ClearBeam performance criteria & next steps

Sara — great, thanks for the clarifications. Short answers then an updated plan: 

- Latency bands: noted. We'll run two measurement bands in the canary: one tuned for Target=300ms and a second relaxed band for Target=400ms with fallback routing enabled (lower-cost model variant).
- Elasticity: we'll include a stepwise scale test to 80 concurrent and a separate spike test to 120 concurrent for 5 minutes to validate the burst SLA.
- KV cache behavior: good question. The SLO matrix assumes a warm-KV baseline; cold-miss penalty for your workload (avg 350 token prompts) empirically adds ~120–180ms at 99th in our test runs. With a pre-warm run (scripted cache-fill) that delta drops below ~40–60ms. We'll include a pre-warm procedure in the runbook.

Updated immediate tasks and owners: 
- Redwood (Alex): deliver one-week canary runbook + measurement script + cost delta (Dedicated vs Hosted) — deliverable: 2027-04-26 09:00 PT.
- Redwood (Karthik): create staging pool & load harness; share Grafana dashboard template and threshold alerts — deliverable: 2027-04-28.
- ClearBeam (Sara): upload sample prompts/dataset + confirm which routes are PII by 2027-04-26 EOD.
- Procurement (ClearBeam): indicate if a dedicated SLA purchase is possible within 30 days (procurement@clearbeam.com).

I'm attaching a lightweight timeline in the runbook that maps measurement windows to dashboard slices so we can confirm pass/fail for each SLO objectively. If that works, we propose kicking off the canary Tue morning (Apr 27) and wrapping initial validation by Apr 30.

— Alex
From: Mike Coleman <mike.coleman@clearbeam.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@clearbeam.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ClearBeam performance criteria & next steps

Quick practical ask from infra/ops before we lock dates: 

- Canary scope: can you confirm whether the canary will exercise the streaming path + long-lived WS connections (we have some workflows that keep sessions open ~12–18 minutes)? We need to make sure session affinity and idle-heartbeat behavior are validated.
- Also: network egress constraints — if you suggest a Dedicated pool, will that preserve the same routing (no extra NAT hop) for our VPC setup? Any change there could add ~30–50ms.

If those two items check out we can provision people for the test window. Prefer a Wed/Thu window if that helps on your side.

On the KV front — we can run a scheduled cache-fill job before spikes, happy to coordinate with your scripts.

— Mike
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 14:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: ClearBeam canary decision criteria (summary)

Alex / Monica — summarizing the thread and proposed decision criteria so we have a clean checklist to hand to Solutions and SRE: 

1) Pass criteria (both must be true):
- Measured 99th latency <= 300ms with warm-KV and pre-warm procedure OR 99th latency <= 400ms with fallback routing enabled.
- Sustained throughput 1,200 req/min with sustained 40 concurrent sessions; elasticity test to 80 concurrent with <10% degradation to tail latency.
- Streaming stability: long-lived WS sessions (12–18m) show <0.5% disconnect rate; token streaming at mean >=250 tokens/sec with no backpressure for 95% of samples.

2) Non-blocking but required signals for go/no-go: SOC2 scope confirmation, procurement intent on committed capacity, and customer-provided sample prompts.

3) Escalation path: if 99th latency >400ms for core interactive flows, propose a short-term mitigation: lower-cost model fallback + progressive rollout (route 10% traffic -> 40% -> 100%) while we optimize kernels and KV placement.

I'll draft the canary runbook steps and hand off to Solutions tomorrow morning. If Alex can attach the run commands and expected dashboard panels to the HubSpot deal, I'll ping CS and SRE to stand by.

— Karthik
